title_en: Provisions of the Supreme People's Court on Several Issues concerning the Application of the Enterprise Bankruptcy Law of the People's Republic of China (III)

articles.content_en: When a People's Court rules to accept a bankruptcy application, the expenses of compulsory liquidation of the company that the debtor has not yet paid, and enforcement expenses such as appraisal fees, announcement fees, and storage fees incurred in enforcement proceedings that have not been concluded, may, by reference to the provisions of the Enterprise Bankruptcy Law on bankruptcy expenses, be paid at any time from the debtor's property. The case acceptance fees and enforcement application fees that the debtor has not yet paid may be satisfied as bankruptcy claims.

After the acceptance of a bankruptcy application, upon approval by a resolution of the creditors' meeting or, before the first creditors' meeting is held, with the permission of the People's Court, the administrator or the self-managing debtor may borrow for the continued business of the debtor. If a creditor who provides the loan claims that it shall be satisfied with priority over ordinary bankruptcy claims by reference to Article 42, Item 4 of the Enterprise Bankruptcy Law, the People's Court shall support such claim; but if it claims priority over claims that have previously been secured by security interests in the debtor's specific property, the People's Court shall not support it. The administrator or the self-managing debtor may create mortgage security for the aforementioned loan. If the mortgaged property has already been mortgaged to other creditors before the acceptance of the bankruptcy application, and the creditor claims satisfaction in the order prescribed in Article 414 of the Civil Code, the People's Court shall support it.

After the acceptance of a bankruptcy application, late fees arising from amounts owed by the debtor, including the doubled interest for delay that the debtor shall pay for failing to perform an effective legal instrument and late fees for labor insurance premiums, if a creditor declares them as bankruptcy claims, the People's Court shall not confirm them.

If a surety is ruled to enter bankruptcy proceedings, the creditor has the right to declare its guarantee claim against the surety. If the principal debt is not due, the guarantee claim is deemed due upon acceptance of the surety's bankruptcy application. If a surety under general suretyship claims to exercise the right of prior action, the People's Court shall not support it, but the creditor's distribution share in the bankruptcy proceedings of the general surety shall be deposited, and after the guarantee liability to be borne by the general surety is determined, distribution shall be made according to the bankruptcy distribution ratio. If the surety is determined to bear the guarantee liability, the administrator of the surety may exercise the right of recourse against the principal debtor or other debtors for the amount actually paid by the surety.

If both the debtor and the surety are ruled to enter bankruptcy proceedings, the creditor has the right to declare claims against the debtor and the surety separately. If the creditor declares all claims against both the debtor and the surety, after it obtains satisfaction from one bankruptcy proceeding, the amount of its claim against the other shall not be adjusted, but the total amount recovered by the creditor shall not exceed the total amount of its claim. After the surety performs the guarantee liability, it shall no longer enjoy the right of recourse.

The administrator shall, in accordance with Article 57 of the Enterprise Bankruptcy Law, register and file the declared claims, recording in detail such matters as the claimant's name, unit, agent, amount of the declared claim, security circumstances, evidence, and contact information, to form a register of claim declarations. The administrator shall, in accordance with Article 57 of the Enterprise Bankruptcy Law, examine such circumstances as the nature, amount, secured property, whether the limitation of action period has expired, and whether the compulsory enforcement period has expired, prepare a schedule of claims, and submit it to the creditors' meeting for verification. During the bankruptcy period, the schedule of claims, the register of claim declarations, and the materials for claim declarations shall be kept by the administrator, and creditors, the debtor, the debtor's employees, and other interested parties have the right to inspect them.

The administrator shall confirm the claim confirmed by an effective legal instrument. If the administrator considers that the claim confirmed by the effective legal instrument on which the creditor relies for declaring the claim is erroneous, or has evidence proving that the creditor and the debtor maliciously fabricated the claim and debt through litigation, arbitration, or notarial documents with compulsory execution effect granted by a notarization authority, it shall, according to law, apply through the trial supervision procedure to the People's Court that rendered the judgment, ruling, or mediation document or to the People's Court at the next higher level to revoke the effective legal instrument, or apply to the People's Court that accepted the bankruptcy application to revoke or not enforce the arbitration award or not enforce the notarized debt document, and then re-determine the claim.

If the debtor or a creditor has an objection to a claim recorded in the schedule of claims, it shall state the reasons and legal basis. If, after the administrator's explanation or adjustment, the objector still disagrees, or the administrator does not explain or adjust, the objector shall, within fifteen days after the verification by the creditors' meeting concludes, initiate an action for confirmation of the claim with the People's Court. If the parties have concluded an arbitration clause or arbitration agreement before the acceptance of the bankruptcy application, they shall apply to the selected arbitration institution for confirmation of the claim-debt relationship.

If the debtor initiates an action with the People's Court on an objection to a claim recorded in the schedule of claims, the objected-against creditor shall be listed as the defendant. If a creditor objects to another person's claim recorded in the schedule, the objected-against creditor shall be listed as the defendant; if a creditor objects to its own claim recorded in the schedule, the debtor shall be listed as the defendant. If there are multiple objectors to the same claim and other objectors apply to participate in the action, they shall be listed as co-plaintiffs.

A single creditor has the right to inspect the report on the debtor's property status, resolutions of the creditors' meeting, resolutions of the creditors' committee, the administrator's supervision report, and other financial and operational information materials of the debtor necessary for participating in the bankruptcy proceedings. If the administrator refuses to provide them without justifiable reasons, the creditor may request the People's Court to make a decision; the People's Court shall make a decision within five days. If the aforementioned information materials involve trade secrets, the creditor shall bear a confidentiality obligation or sign a confidentiality agreement according to law; if they involve state secrets, they shall be handled in accordance with relevant legal provisions.

In addition to on-site voting, resolutions of the creditors' meeting may be voted by non-on-site methods such as correspondence or online voting, after the administrator informs the creditors of the relevant resolution matters in advance. If non-on-site voting is adopted, the administrator shall, within three days after the creditors' meeting is held, inform the creditors who participated in the voting of the voting results by letter, e-mail, announcement, or other means. According to Article 82 of the Enterprise Bankruptcy Law, when group voting is conducted on a draft reorganization plan, creditors or shareholders whose rights and interests are adjusted or affected by the draft reorganization plan have the right to participate in the voting; creditors or shareholders whose rights and interests are not adjusted or affected, by reference to Article 83 of the Enterprise Bankruptcy Law, shall not participate in the voting on the draft reorganization plan.

If a resolution of the creditors' meeting has any of the following circumstances and harms the interests of creditors, and a creditor applies for its revocation, the People's Court shall support it: (1) the convening of the creditors' meeting violates statutory procedures; (2) the voting at the creditors' meeting violates statutory procedures; (3) the content of the resolution of the creditors' meeting is illegal; (4) the resolution of the creditors' meeting exceeds the scope of functions and powers of the creditors' meeting. The People's Court may rule to revoke all or part of the resolutions on matters and order the creditors' meeting to make a new resolution according to law. A creditor applying for revocation of a resolution of the creditors' meeting shall submit a written application. If the creditors' meeting votes by non-on-site methods such as correspondence or online voting, the time limit for the creditor to apply for revocation shall be calculated from the date the creditor receives the notice.

The creditors' meeting may, in accordance with Article 68, Paragraph 1, Item 4 of the Enterprise Bankruptcy Law, entrust the creditors' committee to exercise the functions and powers of the creditors' meeting provided for in Article 61, Paragraph 1, Items 2, 3 and 5 of the Enterprise Bankruptcy Law. The creditors' meeting may not make a general authorization entrusting the creditors' committee to exercise all functions and powers of the creditors' meeting.

A decision of the creditors' committee on a matter under discussion shall be adopted by more than half of all members, and a record of the discussion shall be made. If a member of the creditors' committee has a different opinion on the resolution on the matter under discussion, it shall be recorded in the record. The creditors' committee, when exercising its functions and powers, shall accept the supervision of the creditors' meeting, report its work to the creditors' meeting in a timely and appropriate manner, and accept the guidance of the People's Court.

If the administrator disposes of major property of the debtor provided for in Article 69 of the Enterprise Bankruptcy Law, it shall prepare a property management or realization plan in advance and submit it to the creditors' meeting for voting; if the creditors' meeting does not approve the plan, the administrator shall not dispose of the property. Before implementing the disposal, the administrator shall, in accordance with Article 69 of the Enterprise Bankruptcy Law, report in writing to the creditors' committee or the People's Court ten days in advance. The creditors' committee may, in accordance with Article 68, Paragraph 2 of the Enterprise Bankruptcy Law, require the administrator to make corresponding explanations regarding the disposal act or provide relevant documentary basis. If the creditors' committee considers that the disposal act implemented by the administrator does not conform to the property management or realization plan adopted by the creditors' meeting, it has the right to require the administrator to correct it. If the administrator refuses to correct it, the creditors' committee may request the People's Court to make a decision. If the People's Court considers that the disposal act implemented by the administrator does not conform to the property management or realization plan adopted by the creditors' meeting, it shall order the administrator to cease the disposal act. The administrator shall correct it, or implement it after submitting it to the creditors' meeting for a new vote and approval.

These Provisions shall take effect as of March 28, 2019. If the judicial interpretations on enterprise bankruptcy issued by this Court before the implementation of these Provisions conflict with these Provisions, they shall no longer apply from the date of implementation of these Provisions.
